differences.note: within ~0.3% on R; 2 drives (606 vs 604) lack rpm/SoC channel in my reader; residual k gap likely edge handling (grid origin/midnight/fill)

tolerance: R within 1; CI endpoints within ~1 (week upper 1.1)
fill_note: no-fill drops to 489 drives (speed/SoC/rpm logged at differing cadences) so is not comparable; 2-10 s stable (+-1.5%), 5 s not a driver
mh_vs_poisson: Not a defect: different weighting of strongly heterogeneous bin-specific ratios (bin RR: 55:144, 60:283, 65:40, 70:3.9, 75:4.1, 80:17.8). MH weights by n_hi*n_st/N; Poisson MLE weights by information on log scale (stationary event counts). Estimand differs; report both and heterogeneity, not a single 'the' ratio.
method_concerns: Heterogeneity across SoC bins spans ~4x to ~280x: a common ratio is a weighted summary, not a constant effect; n_hi in bin 55 and 80 tiny (170, 45)
Day bootstrap treats days as iid; ISO-week upper bound is wider (63 vs 57), indicating between-day autocorrelation unmodelled by day resampling; prefer week interval as conservative
Frozen bin set is not re-selected inside bootstrap: eligibility variance omitted (small, bins 55-80 comfortably above 30 except 80 stationary 291/hi 45)
Per-second hazard counts repeated at-risk seconds within a start attempt; k_st is 112 events so stationary rate has wide Poisson uncertainty, which the day bootstrap does capture
Observational: speed band is not randomised; ratio is descriptive (high speed demands power), not causal
language_concerns: describe as estimated per-second start-hazard ratio, not 'measured'; avoid causal wording
